title: Add the quest question record and its ask, answer, withdraw, list and view commands (seq 179a)
description:
opum-doc seq 179 (ODOC-OP-2026-10-03-10), the operator's approval of constitution Articles 4 and 5 as amended. 0.14.0 work, item (a), relayed by opum-agent.

The design is opum-doc's docs/reference/questions-decisions-and-adrs.md and docs/reference/operator-questions-in-quest-design.md, both on opum-doc main. Read them there; this record exists so the item is tracked, not to restate them.

In outline: a `question` record with the full command set -- ask, answer, withdraw, list and view -- and a `via` field recording how an answer arrived. Workers implement exactly what the design says and report issues to opum-doc; they make no design calls.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The question record and its ask, answer, withdraw, list and view commands behave as the opum-doc design specifies
The via field records how an answer arrived, as the design defines it
The machine contract for each new command is documented and its envelope conforms

plan: 1. Domain: Question record type + zod schema + id/validators (src/domain/questions/questions.ts).
2. Port + adapter: QuestionRepository and LocalQuestionRepository, one file per record at .quest/questions/Q-N.json.
3. Application: QuestionService with ask/answer/withdraw/list/view; answer requires --actor-kind human; via recorded from input.
4. CLI: quest question ask|answer|withdraw|list|view dispatch in main.ts + refs-aware nextQuestionId; wire createQuestionService in composition.ts.
5. Contract: manifest name union + entries (command-contract.ts), help entries (command-help.ts), update the manifest golden in test/contract/command-contract.test.ts.
6. Tests: round-trip ask/answer/withdraw/list/view; answer requires human actor; via field; then full check.
implementationNotes: DEC-183 review round 1 at 6670e074 returned REQUEST CHANGES (2 blocking). All six items are addressed in follow-up commits on this branch and re-verified: (1) question list and view now declare the COMPLETE top-level key set (id, createdAt, updatedAt added), and the payload-subset-of-declared check classifies every non-mutating command that declares fields, deriving its population from the manifest so a new family must be classified; (2) the overview guide lists the question family and its guard derives the lifecycle groups from the manifest instead of hardcoding four, with the guide-commands comment corrected; (3) a CHANGELOG entry; (4) the question store now takes the task store's inter-process lock around id allocation and the read-modify-write, returning conflict/exit 5 rather than overwriting, proved by a concurrent-write test that is RED with the lock bypassed (mutation-verified); (5) .quest/questions/ counts in hasOwnedContent, with a test; (6) the suite pins the DEC-190 refusal message names, separates the zero-option case, asserts updatedAt advances on answer and on withdraw, covers double-withdraw, double-answer and a non-option --choice, and readAll wraps a failed read into a quest storage error. A fresh reviewer is spawned at the new head.
finalSummary:
QCLI-445, opum-doc seq 179(a): the CLI half of the operator-question design.

WHAT CHANGED. A new "question" record -- id, title, context, options (key/label/description), recommended, status, answer, createdAt, updatedAt -- stored one record per file at .quest/questions/Q-N.json, plus the quest question ask|answer|withdraw|list|view command group. Q-N allocation is refs-aware, reusing the filename scan against the family's own directory. answer records "via" (how the answer arrived) and REQUIRES --actor-kind human, the CLI half of the design's forgery guard; answer and withdraw are the record's two mutually-exclusive terminal transitions from "open". Machine contract: kinds question.asked/answered/withdrawn/list/view declared in the manifest; question list/view declare the COMPLETE key set; help entries added; the manifest golden updated.

FIELDS THE DESIGN PROSE DOES NOT SPELL OUT, settled by DEC-190 (opum-doc #1000) rather than inferred: (1) a "withdrawal" object holding the required withdraw --reason, a required flag whose value would otherwise be discarded; (2) createdAt/updatedAt, as every other per-file record carries; (3) ask requires 2 to 4 options, with --recommend REQUIRED and naming one of them (a text-only Other answer stays allowed). The board-pane UI and its tool.call guard are QCLI-446 (held, sensitive).

SIZE: 1064 insertions across 13 files as first built, plus the DEC-190 and review-round commits -- one coherent feature (record + commands + proof + contract), stated in the PR body.

DEC-190 (opum-doc #1000) applied before review, per team-lead: withdrawal is {reason, by, at} and is present ONLY when status is withdrawn (absent otherwise); createdAt and updatedAt are carried, with updatedAt advancing on answer and withdraw; ask requires 2 to 4 options and --recommend is REQUIRED and must name one of them, while a text-only answer through the Other row stays allowed. The refusals are record-validation errors on exit 6, named question_options_out_of_range, question_recommend_required and question_recommend_not_an_option.

DEC-183 round 1 requested changes at 6670e074; all six items are addressed: (1) question list/view declare the complete key set and the payload-subset check classifies every non-mutating fields-declaring command, derived from the manifest; (2) the overview guide lists question and its guard derives the groups from the manifest; (3) a CHANGELOG entry; (4) the store takes the task store's inter-process lock around allocation and the read-modify-write, conflict/exit 5 rather than overwrite, mutation-verified; (5) .quest/questions/ counts in hasOwnedContent; (6) the test-hardening set. Round 2 APPROVED; landed as opum-ai/quest-cli#615 (dev f5eb1b88).
